Kinetics (physics)
In
physics
and
engineering
,
kinetics
is the branch of
classical mechanics
that is concerned with the relationship between
motion
and its causes, specifically,
forces
and
torques
.

Since the mid-20th century, the term
dynamics
(or
analytical dynamics
) has largely superseded
kinetics
in
physics
textbooks,
[
4
]
though the term is still used in
engineering
and
biomechanics
[
5
]
.
In
plasma physics
, kinetics refers to the study of
continua
in
velocity
space. This is usually in the context of non-thermal (
non-Maxwellian
) velocity distributions, or processes that
perturb
thermal distributions. These "
kinetic plasmas
" cannot be adequately described with
fluid equations
.
The term
kinetics
is also used to refer to
chemical kinetics
, particularly in
chemical physics
and
physical chemistry
.
